open_points.subject: A11 Required tests INV-17
open_points.text: a project holding only dates without an offset passes
open_points.question: Does a `photo_date` ending in `Z` count as a date without an offset that passes, or as the old date that normative rule 1 says must stop delivery?
options: `Z` is an offset indicator, so the project stops
Only `+HH:MM` and `-HH:MM` are offsets, so a `Z` date passes
open_points.default_guess: Treat `Z` as an offset indicator and stop the project, following normative rule 1.

events: The calling flow reads the project's staff photo list before delivery.
outcomes: The flow classifies the `Z` date as old and places and publishes nothing.
The flow treats the date as being without an offset, lets the project pass, and continues delivery.
witness.observer: The owner and anyone receiving the delivered photo

open_points.subject: A11 Required tests INV-17
open_points.text: a project holding only dates without an offset passes
open_points.question: Which representations qualify as dates without an offset, and does “passes” mean only that the old-date gate accepts them or that the calling flow must proceed with delivery?
options: Only valid timezone-naive datetime representations pass the old-date gate
Any value not ending in `Z`, `+HH:MM`, or `-HH:MM` passes the old-date gate
The test must demonstrate that delivery proceeds, not merely that this gate accepts the list
open_points.default_guess: Require valid timezone-naive date representations and interpret “passes” as passing only the old-date gate.

witness.initial: A project's list contains `2026-11-20`, `2026-11-20T10:00:00`, or a malformed value such as `not-a-date`.
events: The calling flow evaluates the list using the A11 rule.
outcomes: Only a valid timezone-naive datetime is accepted; date-only or malformed values cause refusal.
Every value lacking one of the listed suffixes is accepted by the old-date check.
witness.observer: The owner and the calling-flow test suite

open_points.subject: A11 Required tests INV-17
open_points.text: a project holding a date with an offset is detected before delivery
open_points.question: What must the witness assert to demonstrate INV-17: detection alone, prevention of publication, prevention of both placement and publication, or the calling flow's reported repair message?
options: Assert only that the detector identifies the offset date
Assert end-to-end that no delivered photo is published
Assert that neither placement nor publication occurs
Also assert that the owner is told which project needs repair
open_points.default_guess: Assert end-to-end that neither placement nor publication occurs and that the owner is told which project needs repair.

witness.initial: A project has a staff photo date ending in `+01:00`.
events: The witness invokes the pre-delivery detection check.
The calling flow would otherwise place and publish a photo.
outcomes: The test passes after asserting only that the date was detected.
The test passes only after asserting that the flow placed and published nothing.
witness.observer: A reviewer relying on the witness to establish INV-17

open_points.subject: A11 Required tests INV-17
open_points.text: The calling flow's own stop is shown when that flow exists.
open_points.question: If no calling flow exists when the witness is assembled, must a later test show its stop once it exists, must the invariant witness fail as incomplete, or is detector-only evidence permanently sufficient?
options: The witness is incomplete until an existing calling flow's stop is shown
Detector-only evidence is sufficient when assembly occurs before the flow exists
A later state must add the calling-flow assertion when the flow is introduced
open_points.default_guess: Require a later calling-flow assertion as soon as the flow exists, and do not treat detector-only evidence as the final witness for the flow-level invariant.

witness.initial: The offset-date detector exists, but no calling-flow implementation exists when its witness is first resolved.
events: The detector's test shows that an offset date is recognized.
A calling flow is implemented later without an explicit stop assertion in its tests.
outcomes: The invariant remains accepted because the flow did not exist when the original witness was resolved.
The invariant becomes incomplete until a test demonstrates the new flow's own stop.
witness.observer: The assembly gate and a maintainer reviewing delivery safety
